# Discussion

**What the surprise is.** The interesting finding is not that a 270M
model fails the behavioral \(a\)/\(an\) demo---@hanna2026latent already
place reliable success at larger scales. The surprise is the
**juxtaposition** inside editable mechanisms. Dual-effect features are
easy to move as *packages*: selection ablation, dose--response, dual
lock, and twin tetrads all agree that free generation yields legal
article--noun switches rather than content-preserving wrappers. The same
handles---plus Latent-Planning-style per-noun features and a dense
residual MLP-in steer---still fail as independent content dials once
\(b\) is held fixed with content interventions kept on. Packaging and
\(b\to c\) are easy to edit; modular \(C\to c\) is not.

**Methodological implication.** Article-only attribution and free
generation overstate modular planning whenever noun changes can be
explained by \(b\to c\). Edge tests that paste native \(b\) while keeping
content edits active, and that score within-class rewrites rather than
any noun change, should be standard before claiming separable
forward/backward planning from feature interventions.

**Relation to Latent Planning.** We do not claim their large-model
results are wrong, nor that latent planning is impossible. On this small
model, dual-effect / content-attributed interventions are better explained
as H2 packagers than as H1 modular planners: what is editable does not
decompose into independent \(C\to c\).
